title: DLMF 24.14 Sums: Let m+n be even with m and n nonzero. Then
summary: DLMF 24.14 Sums: Let m+n be even with m and n nonzero. Then
body: NIST DLMF section 24.14 (Sums) says: "Let m+n be even with m and n nonzero. Then In the following two identities, valid for n\geq 2 , the sums are taken over all nonnegative integers j,k,\ell with j+k+\ell=n . In the next identity, valid for n\geq 4 , the sum is taken over all positive integers j,k,\ell,m with j+k+\ell+m=n . For ( 24.14.11 ) and ( 24.14.12 ), see Al-Salam and Carlitz ( 1959 ) . These identities can be regarded as higher-order recurrences. Let \det[a_{r+s}] denote a Hankel (or persymmetric ) determinant , that is, an (n+1)\times(n+1) determinant with element a_{r+s} in row r and column s for r,s=0,1,\dots,n . Then For other sums involving Bernoulli and Euler numbers and polynomials see Hansen ( 1975 , pp. 331–347) and Prudnikov et al. ( 1990 , pp. 383–386) ." Equation 24.14.7 on the page has alt text "\sum_{j=0}^{m}\sum_{k=0}^{n}\genfrac{(}{)}{0.0pt}{}{m}{j}\genfrac{(}{)}{0.0pt}% {}{n}{k}\frac{B_{j}B_{k}}{m+n-j-k+1}=(-1)^{m-1}\frac{m!n!}{(m+n)!}B_{m+n}.". Equation 24.14.10 on the page has alt text "\sum\frac{(2n)!}{(2j)!(2k)!(2\ell)!(2m)!}B_{2j}B_{2k}B_{2\ell}B_{2m}=-{2n+3% \choose 3}B_{2n}-\frac{4}{3}n^{2}(2n-1)B_{2n-2}.". This card records that section's wording and equation alt text. It does not retypeset a formula the alt text did not carry.
